subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 30-year-old woman at 24 weeks gestation has routine laboratory studies. Her physician notes that renal function changes markedly in pregnancy, with a substantial increase in glomerular filtration rate.
question: Which of the following laboratory changes is expected as a result of the increased GFR in pregnancy?

options.text: Elevated serum creatinine with reduced GFR

explanation_correct: Pregnancy increases GFR, which lowers serum BUN and creatinine. This is a normal physiologic change and should not be mistaken for renal disease. Mild glucosuria and proteinuria may also occur. The rise in GFR is one of several renal adaptations of pregnancy, alongside hydronephrosis and hydroureter.

explanation_incorrect.A: GFR rises in pregnancy, so BUN and creatinine fall rather than rise.
explanation_incorrect.B: Pregnancy does not reduce GFR; creatinine is typically decreased, not elevated.
explanation_incorrect.C: Uric acid is not the marker primarily affected by the pregnancy-related rise in GFR described here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hypercalcemia is not a consequence of increased GFR in pregnancy.

educationalObjective: Increased GFR in pregnancy lowers BUN and creatinine.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks has renal ultrasound for flank pain. The study shows dilation of the renal pelvis and ureter, which her physician says is a common physiologic finding in pregnancy.
question: The physiologic hydronephrosis and hydroureter of pregnancy are typically more prominent on which side?

options.text: Only on the left in the third trimester
Neither side; it is always pathologic

explanation_correct: Physiologic hydronephrosis and hydroureter occur in pregnancy and are more prominent on the right side. This asymmetry relates in part to compression of the right ureter by the gravid uterus and anatomic differences. It is a normal finding that generally resolves postpartum. Recognizing it as physiologic prevents unnecessary intervention.

explanation_incorrect.A: The dilation is typically more prominent on the right, not the left.
explanation_incorrect.C: The changes are characteristically asymmetric, more pronounced on the right.
explanation_incorrect.D: The right side is more affected; stating it occurs only on the left is incorrect.
explanation_incorrect.E: Mild hydronephrosis and hydroureter are normal physiologic changes in pregnancy, not always pathologic.

educationalObjective: Pregnancy-related hydronephrosis and hydroureter are more prominent on the right.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 32-year-old woman at 30 weeks gestation notices dark patches on her cheeks and a dark vertical line on her abdomen. She asks whether these are normal pregnancy changes.
question: Which of the following cutaneous findings is a normal physiologic change of pregnancy?
explanation_correct: Melasma, linea nigra, areola darkening, striae gravidarum, varicose veins, and palmar erythema are normal skin changes of pregnancy. Melasma produces hyperpigmented patches on the face, and linea nigra is a dark line along the abdomen. These changes are benign and usually fade after delivery. A malar rash suggests an autoimmune process rather than a normal pregnancy change.

explanation_incorrect.A: A malar rash is associated with systemic lupus erythematosus, not a normal pregnancy skin change.
explanation_incorrect.B: Erythema nodosum is a panniculitis, not a physiologic pregnancy change.
explanation_incorrect.D: Urticaria is not among the listed normal pregnancy skin changes.
explanation_incorrect.E: Petechiae are not a normal physiologic skin change of pregnancy.

educationalObjective: Melasma, linea nigra, areola darkening, striae, varicose veins, and palmar erythema are normal pregnancy skin changes.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A woman in her third trimester reports new difficulty with bowel movements and occasional heartburn. Her obstetrician attributes these to normal gastrointestinal changes of pregnancy.
question: Which of the following gastrointestinal symptoms is common in pregnancy?
explanation_correct: Constipation, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and gallstones are recognized gastrointestinal changes of pregnancy. Progesterone-mediated smooth muscle relaxation slows intestinal transit and lowers lower esophageal sphincter tone, contributing to constipation and reflux. These symptoms are common and generally managed conservatively. Diarrhea and gastrointestinal bleeding are not typical normal changes.

explanation_incorrect.A: Diarrhea is not one of the typical GI changes of pregnancy; constipation is more common.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hematemesis indicates upper GI bleeding, not a normal pregnancy change.
explanation_incorrect.C: Melena indicates gastrointestinal bleeding, not a normal pregnancy change.
explanation_incorrect.E: Dysphagia is not a listed common GI change of pregnancy.

educationalObjective: Constipation, GERD, and gallstones are common GI changes in pregnancy.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A pregnant woman at 26 weeks has a hemoglobin of 11 g/dL. Her physician explains that a mild anemia is expected because plasma volume expands more than red cell mass.
question: Which hematologic change is expected in a normal pregnancy?

options.text: Iron-deficiency anemia from decreased micronutrient needs

explanation_correct: Pregnancy causes a dilutional, or physiologic, anemia because plasma volume increases disproportionately to red blood cell mass. A hypercoagulable state also develops, and micronutrient requirements increase. The dilutional anemia is a normal finding and is distinct from true iron-deficiency anemia. Hemoglobin typically improves postpartum.

explanation_incorrect.B: Pancytopenia is not a normal pregnancy change and suggests bone marrow pathology.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polycythemia is the opposite of the expected dilutional anemia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hemophilia is a coagulation factor deficiency, not a normal pregnancy change; pregnancy is actually hypercoagulable.
explanation_incorrect.E: Micronutrient requirements increase, not decrease, in pregnancy.

educationalObjective: Normal pregnancy features dilutional anemia, a hypercoagulable state, and increased micronutrient needs.
source: Generated from 15. Reproductive.pdf - Physiology: Physiologic changes in pregnancy

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A pregnant woman has thyroid function tests showing an elevated total T4 with a normal free T4. Her physician explains that pregnancy alters binding protein concentrations as part of its endocrine adaptations.
question: Which of the following endocrine changes occurs in pregnancy?
explanation_correct: Pregnancy increases the binding proteins TBG, CBG, and SHBG, which raises total hormone levels while free hormone levels remain regulated. Other endocrine adaptations include increased insulin resistance and insulin secretion, increased lipolysis and fat utilization, and pituitary enlargement. The rise in TBG explains the elevated total T4 with a normal free T4 in pregnancy. These changes support the metabolic demands of the gravid state.

explanation_incorrect.A: Insulin resistance increases, not decreases, in pregnancy.
explanation_incorrect.B: Lipolysis and fat utilization increase, not decrease, in pregnancy.
explanation_incorrect.C: The pituitary enlarges in pregnancy; it does not shrink.
explanation_incorrect.D: TBG, CBG, and SHBG increase, not decrease, in pregnancy.

educationalObjective: Pregnancy raises TBG/CBG/SHBG and insulin resistance, and enlarges the pituitary.
